- In  order  to  progress  the  city  measures,  progress  is  managed  based  on  the  'Hiroshima  City  Environment Management System' that has been uniquely developed by the city.
- The conduct status of each year will be published on the city website.
extraction_rationale: This is a governance and accountability policy for climate implementation. It qualifies as a policy because it establishes monitoring and disclosure procedures.

policy_statement: The city will establish a Low-carbon City Development Citizens Conference to coordinate action among citizens, businesses, and administrators.
source_quote: - By  preparing  this  plan,  'Low-carbon  City  Development  Citizens  Conference  (tentative)'  representing  citizens, business operators and administrators, etc., is established as a system to take actions together.
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete institutional arrangement for plan implementation. It qualifies as a policy because it creates a coordination body for climate action.

policy_statement: The city will review and revise the plan and greenhouse gas reduction targets in FY2020 based on domestic, international, and socioeconomic changes.
source_quote: In the short-term target year in this plan (FY2020), the achievement status of measures will be evaluated, and directions of  measures  and  reduction  target  of  greenhouse  effect  gases,  etc.  will  be  revised  based  on  the  domestic  and international changes concerning global warming as well as social economic changes, and then the plan will be changed or the next plan will be prepared.
extraction_rationale: This is a policy because it commits to periodic review and revision of climate targets and measures. It is procedural but still a formal planning commitment.

policy_statement: Hong Kong will achieve carbon neutrality before 2050 and reduce total carbon emissions by half from the 2005 level before 2035.
source_quote:
We are delighted to present the Hong Kong's Climate Action Plan 2050 which sets the vision of 'Zero-carbon Emissions  · Liveable City · Sustainable Development', and commits to a more aggressive medium-term target to reduce total carbon emissions of Hong Kong by half against the 2005 level before 2035.

The Chief Executive, Mrs Carrie Lam, announced Hong Kong's carbon neutrality target in the 2020 Policy Address
extraction_rationale: This is a clear, quantified climate commitment with deadlines. It is a standalone overarching target rather than a sub-action under a named initiative.

policy_statement: The Government will invest HK$240 billion over the next 15 to 20 years to support climate change actions, including renewable energy, energy efficiency, electrification of transport, and waste management.
source_quote: In the next 15 to 20 years, the Government will be investing another HK$240 billion to support a series of actions to combat climate change. Major actions will include developing distributed renewable energy, managing energy demand  including  enhancing  energy  efficiency  and  conservation  in  both  new  and  existing  buildings,  decarbonising  the  vehicle  fleet  to  reach  zero  vehicular  emissions,  and  transforming  our  waste  management system to cease landfilling of municipal wastes, etc.
extraction_rationale: This is a committed public investment line with a stated amount and time horizon, directly tied to climate actions.

policy_statement: Hong Kong will strive to achieve carbon neutrality before 2050.
source_quote:
To this end, the Chief Executive announced in her 2020 Policy Address that Hong Kong would strive to achieve carbon neutrality before 2050.

The Hong Kong's Climate Action Plan 2050 is the fourth major environmental policy plan published this year. It brings together the overall strategies, plans, targets and actions for Hong Kong to achieve carbon neutrality before 2050.
extraction_rationale: This is a direct, high-level climate target with a deadline. It is repeated elsewhere but remains a valid policy commitment.

policy_statement: Hong Kong will set out more proactive strategies and measures to reduce carbon emissions.
source_quote: The community in general expects Hong Kong to go further in deep decarbonisation… The Hong Kong Special Administrative Region will strive to achieve carbon neutrality before 2050. To this end, the Government will set out more proactive strategies and measures to reduce carbon emissions.
extraction_rationale: This is a policy commitment to adopt further measures, though it is somewhat broad and non-specific. It qualifies because it is an explicit governmental commitment to action.

policy_statement: Hong Kong will use zero-carbon energy extensively for electricity generation to achieve carbon neutrality before 2050.
source_quote: Our top priority is to make careful planning so that Hong Kong can use zero-carbon energy for electricity generation extensively and achieve carbon neutrality before 2050. Not only will this address about two-thirds of the current carbon emissions in Hong Kong, it will also provide zero-carbon energy to an electrified transport system.
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete strategic commitment to transform electricity supply, a core mitigation policy.

policy_statement: Hong Kong will set more stringent energy efficiency standards and enhance energy efficiency in both new and existing buildings.
source_quote:
As for the remaining carbon emissions of less than 10%, they would be dealt with through the development and application of low-carbon technologies.

As for the remaining carbon emissions of less than 10%, they would be dealt with through the development and application of low-carbon technologies. We must set more stringent energy efficiency standards,  enhance  the  energy  efficiency  of both new and existing buildings, and enlist the full support of various sectors in the society to save energy and reduce waste.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific energy-efficiency commitment with a clear mechanism, even though the wording is broad.

policy_statement: Indonesia will monitor, review, and update its Long-Term Strategy for Low Carbon and Climate Resilience 2050 as necessary, taking into account national circumstances, capacity and capability, and the Paris Agreement.
source_quote: The Indonesia's LTS-LCCR 2050 reflects the most recent data and information, analysis, and scenario for possible future in order to contribute the global climate actions in achieving Paris Agreement's goal. As a developing country, Indonesia will likely experience dynamic changes due to national and global changes as well as current COVID-19 pandemic. In this regard, the Indonesia's LTS-LCCR 2050 will be monitored, reviewed and updated, as necessary, taking into consideration national circumstances, capacity and capability, and the provision under the Paris Agreement.
extraction_rationale: This is a clear policy commitment to an ongoing review-and-update process for the national climate strategy. It is a governance/planning commitment rather than a financial instrument.

policy_statement: Indonesia will implement a long-term low-carbon and climate-resilient strategy through mitigation and adaptation pathways, with sectoral and regional actions aligned to the Paris Agreement and national development objectives.
source_quote: Indonesia submits Long-Term Strategy for Low Carbon and Climate Resilience 2050, which aims to contribute to global goal and to achieve national development objectives, taking into consideration the balance between emission reduction, economic growth, justice and climate resilience development. The LTS-LCCR 2050 also reflects the mandate Indonesian Constitution (UUD 45) Article 28 H on the state obligation to guarantee decent life and healthy environment for all citizens.
extraction_rationale: This is the umbrella strategy for the whole document and is supported by multiple sub-actions later in the text. It qualifies as a parent policy because it establishes the overarching climate policy framework.

policy_statement: Indonesia will increase ambition on greenhouse gas reduction by peaking national emissions in 2030, achieving a forest and land-use net sink, reaching 540 Mton CO2e by 2050, and exploring net-zero emissions in 2060 or sooner.

extraction_rationale: This is a quantified national emissions target with deadlines, which clearly qualifies as a climate policy commitment.

policy_statement: Indonesia will increase renewable energy, improve energy efficiency, reduce coal consumption, and implement CCS, CCUS, and BECCS in the energy sector to achieve its long-term mitigation target.

extraction_rationale: This is a concrete sectoral mitigation commitment with named interventions and technologies. It is not merely descriptive because it states the actions needed to achieve the target.

policy_statement: Indonesia will pursue adaptation pathways that reduce climate change impacts on national GDP loss by 3.45% in 2050 through increased resilience in food, water, energy, and environmental health.

extraction_rationale: This is a quantified adaptation target tied to resilience outcomes and therefore qualifies as a policy commitment.

extraction_rationale: This is a planning commitment for adaptation implementation through named pathways and coordination. It is policy-relevant even though it is framed at a high level.

extraction_rationale: This is a specific quantified commitment tied to the Joint Crediting Mechanism and the use of credits for NDC achievement. It is a policy instrument/implementation mechanism rather than a mere background statement.

policy_statement: Japan will establish and implement the Joint Crediting Mechanism to quantify emission reductions and removals achieved through diffusion of decarbonizing technologies and measures in developing countries, and use those contributions to achieve its NDC.
source_quote: Japan will establish and implement the Joint Crediting Mechanism (JCM) in order to quantitatively evaluate contributions of Japan to greenhouse gas emission reductions and removals which are achieved through the diffusion of, among others, leading decarbonizing technologies, products, systems, services, and infrastructures as well as through the implementation of measures in developing countries and others, and in order to use such contributions to achieve Japan's NDC. By doing so, through public-private collaborations, Japan aims to secure accumulated emission reductions and removals at the level of approximately 100 million t-CO 2 by fiscal year 2030.
section_header: 5. Assumptions and methodological approaches, including those for estimating and accounting for anthropogenic greenhouse gas emissions and, as appropriate, removals:
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete implementation mechanism under Article 6 with a quantified contribution target. It qualifies as a policy because it establishes a named program and a specific use of credits toward the NDC.

policy_statement: Japan will make proactive efforts in international cooperation to promote decarbonization and improve resilience in developing countries, including by developing policies and institutional platforms and facilitating technology diffusion.
source_quote: Furthermore, Japan will also make proactive efforts in the area of international cooperation to promote decarbonization and to improve resilience in developing countries and others, including from developing policies and institutional platforms to promoting sector- and city-level efforts as well as facilitating technology diffusion.
section_header: 5. Assumptions and methodological approaches, including those for estimating and accounting for anthropogenic greenhouse gas emissions and, as appropriate, removals:
extraction_rationale: This is a stated international cooperation commitment with specific implementation channels. It is somewhat broad, but still qualifies because it names deliberate actions and institutional development.

policy_statement: Japan will promote policies contributing to growth by holding decarbonization as its pillar.
source_quote: For those targets to be achieved, Japan will promote policies contributing to growth by holding decarbonization as its pillar.
section_header: (a) (ii) b Best practices and experience related to the preparation of the nationally determined contribution;
extraction_rationale: This is a broad strategic commitment linking policy direction to decarbonization. It is less specific than other entries, but still a governing commitment to pursue decarbonization-centered policy.

policy_statement: Japan will put forward all possible efforts in all areas including thorough energy efficiency measures, maximum introduction of renewable energy, and decarbonization of public sectors and local communities.
source_quote: In order to create a virtuous cycle of the economy and the environment and to realize robust growth toward its ambitious goal for fiscal year 2030, Japan will put forward all possible efforts in all areas including by thorough energy efficiency measures, maximum introduction of renewable energy, as well as decarbonization of public sectors and local communities.
section_header: (a) (ii) b Best practices and experience related to the preparation of the nationally determined contribution;
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete policy direction naming specific interventions: energy efficiency, renewable energy, and decarbonization of public sectors and local communities. It is a policy commitment even though not quantified.

policy_statement: Japan will enhance productivity and ensure sustainability in food, agriculture, forestry, and fisheries through innovation under the Strategy for Sustainable Food Systems, MeaDRI.
source_quote: In food, agriculture, forestry, and fisheries industries, based on the 'Strategy for Sustainable Food Systems, MeaDRI (Measures for achievement of Decarbonization and Resilience with Innovation) (decided by Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries on May 12 th , 2021),' Japan aims to enhance productivity potentials and ensure sustainability in a compatible manner through innovation.
section_header: (a) (ii) b Best practices and experience related to the preparation of the nationally determined contribution;
extraction_rationale: This references a named strategy and a concrete implementation direction in a major sector. The climate linkage is somewhat indirect because the quoted goal emphasizes productivity and sustainability, but the strategy name explicitly includes decarbonization and resilience.

policy_statement: Japan will steadily carry out cross-sectoral decarbonization efforts in national land, urban, and regional spheres under MLIT's Green Challenge.
source_quote: Based on the 'MLIT's Green Challenge (decided by Ministry of Land, Infrastructure, Transport and Tourism on July 6 th , 2021),' Japan will steadily carry out efforts in cross-sectoral decarbonization in national land, urban and regional spheres.
section_header: (a) (ii) b Best practices and experience related to the preparation of the nationally determined contribution;
extraction_rationale: This is a named initiative with a specific implementation commitment to cross-sectoral decarbonization. It qualifies as a policy because it is an operational program rather than background context.

policy_statement: Japan will create new industries and jobs by advancing strategic transitions to a circular economy and through nature-based solutions.
source_quote: Japan will create new industries and jobs by proceeding efforts in strategic transitions to a circular economy, which is necessary for decarbonization, as well as through nature-based solutions (NbS).
section_header: (a) (ii) b Best practices and experience related to the preparation of the nationally determined contribution;
extraction_rationale: This is a strategic commitment to pursue circular-economy transitions and NbS. It is policy-relevant because it names deliberate transitions and implementation pathways, though the climate objective is partly embedded in broader economic framing.

policy_statement: Japan will transform its economy and society into sustainable and resilient socio-economic systems by positioning decarbonization as one of the main issues in all socio-economic activities.
source_quote: It is therefore essential to position decarbonization as one of the main issues in all socio-economic activities and to bring forward the transformation into sustainable and resilient socio-economic systems.
section_header: (a) (ii) b Best practices and experience related to the preparation of the nationally determined contribution;
extraction_rationale: This is a broad strategic policy direction centered on decarbonization and systemic transformation. It is not highly specific, but it is a clear government commitment.

policy_statement: Japan will continue progress management for its new 2030 target in the same manner as its existing Plan for Global Warming Countermeasures, including evaluation of measures and identification of delayed sections.
source_quote: Also, with regard to the new target for fiscal year 2030, the Government will continue progress management in a similar manner as mentioned in the above.
section_header: (a) (ii) b Best practices and experience related to the preparation of the nationally determined contribution;
extraction_rationale: This is a governance and implementation commitment to monitor and manage progress toward the target. It qualifies as policy because it specifies an ongoing administrative mechanism.

policy_statement: The Government of Kuwait, represented by the Environment Public Authority (EPA), has committed itself to ensure the implementation of its National Adaptation Plan (NAP), in partnership with other governmental and non-governmental institutions.
source_quote: The Government of Kuwait, represented by the Environment Public Authority (EPA), has committed itself to ensure the implementation of its National Adaptation Plan (NAP), in partnership with other governmental and non-governmental institutions, furthermore A national coordination mechanism has been identified to implement a range of national initiatives to protect the various vital sectors from the Negative impacts of climate change. Therefore, future programs have been developed to deal with the various risks face the sectors and across time periods.
extraction_rationale: This is a clear governmental commitment to implement the NAP through coordination with other institutions. It is policy-like because it establishes implementation responsibility and a coordination mechanism, though it is broad rather than a single discrete measure.

policy_statement: Kuwait's National Adaptation Plan aims to build adaptive capacity and resilience and to integrate climate change adaptation into policies, programs, and activities across relevant sectors.
source_quote:
The main objectives of establishing the NAP process in Kuwait are to:

- a) build  an  adaptive  plan  with  capacity  and  resilience  that  can  reduce vulnerability to the climate change impacts; and
- b) facilitate  and  integrate  the  adaptation  of  climate  change  into  policies, programs,  and  activities,  in  specific  development  planning  strategies and processes, within all national relevant sector.
section_header: 1.6. Process and methodology of establishing the NAP
extraction_rationale: This is a direct policy objective with a defined outcome and implementation direction. It qualifies as a climate policy because it sets national adaptation goals and mainstreaming commitments.

policy_statement: Kuwait will use the NAP process to promote policies, strengthen institutional frameworks, improve cooperation and coordination, and facilitate access to information and technology for local populations.
section_header: 1.3. The need for National Adaptation Plan (NAP)
extraction_rationale: Although framed as UNFCCC objectives, the text explicitly states the policy direction Kuwait is adopting through the NAP process. It is a planning and institutional policy commitment.

policy_statement: Kuwait's NAP process will be based on national priorities, stakeholder consultation, and iterative review and updating.
section_header: 1.3. The need for National Adaptation Plan (NAP)
extraction_rationale: This is a procedural policy commitment because it specifies how adaptation planning will be conducted and implemented. It is not a standalone project, but it is still a governing commitment.

policy_statement: Kuwait will prepare and implement a National Adaptation Plan that includes short-term and long-term programs and projects to adapt to climate change.
source_quote:
This document represents guidelines of the national actions needed to adapt to climate change  in  Kuwait.  The  overall  objective  of  the  National  Adaptation  Plan  (NAP)  is  to provide  an  integrated  development  plan  and  subsequent  programmes  targeting  local .

communities and environmental components in areas under the threat of climate change The NAP is prepared in accordance with the UNFCCC directives and articles and includes a detailed survey of the environment and the most affected areas and sectors in climate change, detailed analysis pertaining to climate change vulnerability, and gaps in each sector to adapt to climate change. Subsequently, programmes and projects are to be initiated in the short term and in the long term to adapt to climate change in the country.
extraction_rationale: This is a direct national planning commitment with implementation through programs and projects. It qualifies as policy because it establishes an integrated adaptation plan and action pipeline.

policy_statement: Kuwait will develop and use a national coordination mechanism and seek partnerships and technical assistance to implement adaptation programs and reduce climate-related side effects.
source_quote: The implementation of the NAP is not the responsibility of EPA alone. Where Adaptation to climate change requires the work of all stakeholders and integration in the design and implementation of initiatives in  several  sectors,  including  water,  coastal  areas,  the  marine  environment,  human  health  and  others. Therefore, EPA will seek technical assistance from international organizations, industrial community and other stakeholders to implement the proposed programs to adapt to climate change and reduce the side effects associated with socio-economic problems.
extraction_rationale: This is a coordination and implementation commitment with clear institutional action. It is policy-relevant because it establishes governance arrangements for adaptation delivery.

policy_statement: Kuwait will monitor climate change continuously through an ongoing environmental data and information program in partnership with stakeholders.
source_quote: One of the expected results is a comprehensive ongoing monitoring program through the necessary environmental data and information to monitor climate change and assess its impact on the State of Kuwait on an ongoing basis, In partnership with all stakeholders such as the academia, private sector and nongovernmental actors in the areas of adaptation to climate change.
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete monitoring commitment tied to adaptation planning. It qualifies as policy because it establishes an ongoing program and stakeholder partnership.

policy_statement: Kuwait will implement climate change adaptation through a participatory national plan while maintaining EPA coordination and oversight.
source_quote: This will be achieved in the manner of implementing the national plan which is based on participation, while maintaining the coordination and oversight role of the EPA in the various activities and initiatives that aim to reach the desired goal to reduce the Negative impacts of climate change and adopt with it.
extraction_rationale: This is a governance commitment describing how adaptation actions will be implemented and overseen. It is policy-like because it assigns institutional roles and implementation principles.

policy_statement: Kuwait will use the NAP process to initiate and launch adaptation planning, stocktake information, address capacity gaps, assess vulnerabilities, and integrate adaptation into development planning.
source_quote:
The UNFCCC technical guidelines for the national adaptation plan process is proposed to be followed in the preparation of the NAP process framework and roadmap. The main objectives of establishing the NAP process in Kuwait are to:

- a) build  an  adaptive  plan  with  capacity  and  resilience  that  can  reduce vulnerability to the climate change impacts; and
- b) facilitate  and  integrate  the  adaptation  of  climate  change  into  policies, programs,  and  activities,  in  specific  development  planning  strategies and processes, within all national relevant sector.
section_header: 1.6. Process and methodology of establishing the NAP
extraction_rationale: This is a broad planning commitment with multiple concrete planning functions. It qualifies as policy because it directs national adaptation planning and mainstreaming.

policy_statement: Kuwait will use a structured methodology to analyze climate change, assess vulnerabilities, identify adaptation needs, prioritize actions, and produce a draft NAP for endorsement and stakeholder communication.
source_quote: The methodology used in this report focuses on the real planning activities, which are comprised  of  Elements  A  and  B  of  the  NAP  process,  they  include  (a)  initiating  and launching NAP process; (b) stocktaking and synthesizing the available information and data on climate change impacts, vulnerability, adaptation in addition to assessing gaps and needs of the enabling environment, (c) addressing capacity gaps and weaknesses in undertaking the NAP process, (d) analyzing current climate and future climate scenarios; (e) assessing vulnerabilities; (f) identifying, reviewing and appraising adaptation options and (g) compiling and communicating national adaptation plan.
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete procedural commitment for national adaptation planning. It qualifies as policy because it specifies the steps Kuwait will follow to develop the NAP.

policy_statement: Kuwait will monitor and evaluate the NAP and use feedback to modify programs, set priorities, and adjust implementation based on local needs.
source_quote:
Monitoring and evaluation of the plan and subsequent impacts of interventions from the different programmes are future objectives and tasks of

the Kuwait Environment Public Authority. This is a very important task as it provides a feedback mechanism for modification of programmes, setting priorities and implementation of activities based on the needs and requirements of local communities in most affected areas.
extraction_rationale: This is a clear implementation and review commitment. It qualifies as policy because it establishes ongoing evaluation and adaptive management of the plan.

policy_statement: Kuwait will use climate vulnerability assessment and climate vulnerability index methods to identify risks, prioritize sectors, and inform adaptation planning.
source_quote: Kuwait NAP was set based on a Climate Vulnerability Assessment (CVA) and a Climate Vulnerability Index (CVI) at strategy level targeting the main four sectors identified in Kuwait Second National Communication Report to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (SNC). Those sectors are marine life and fisheries, water resources, coastal zones, and human health. Kuwait CVA's objectives are to identify  and  understand  historical  and  projected  climate  risks  at  the  country  level,  to  evaluate  sectoral climate risks to inform sector planning, and to identify gaps for conducting climate vulnerability index.
extraction_rationale: This is a methodological policy commitment because it establishes the analytical basis for adaptation planning. It is not a project, but it is a deliberate planning instrument.

policy_statement: Kuwait will prepare sectoral action plans for adaptation and mobilize financial resources for technology transfer and implementation of adaptation measures.
source_quote: The important conclusions that can be drawn from the analysis are the high level of interest at the national level to enhance national and sectoral capacities to adapt to climate change and its induced disasters.  The climate change and the variations among years, the high vulnerability of four main sectors and the adverse impacts of the different climate change scenario are of high concerns to decision-makers in the country. Therefore, the report had included many recommendations for adaptation at sectoral and national levels. In  summary,  the  Action  Plan  recommends  the  preparation  of  sectoral  action  plan  for  adaptation  with emphasis on the four main sectors. Mobilization of financial resources, therefore, is urgently needed for technology transfer and for implementing the proposed adaptation measures.
extraction_rationale: This is a direct policy recommendation with implementation and financing implications. It qualifies because it calls for sectoral plans and resource mobilization, though it is framed as a recommendation.

policy_statement: Kuwait will implement legislation and regulation to limit vehicle exhaust emissions and encourage unleaded fuel consumption.
source_quote:
The results of the study showed that the rate of HC, CO and NOx emissions in Kuwait is higher than the emission in the US. Owing to this study and others following, legislative and regulation on the limit of  exhaust a car  can emit were put in place, and thus vehicles were adjusted during maintenance   (E. Al Bassam and A. Khan, 2004).

Since signing into the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change, Kuwait has  introduced  new  policies  and  rules  concerning  the  emission  of  gases  into  the atmosphere. Kuwait also encouraged the consumption of unleaded fuel by decreasing its price compared to the leaded fuel; also, the number of gas stations offering the leaded option is very few.
extraction_rationale: This is a regulatory emissions policy with a clear mitigation mechanism. It qualifies because it imposes emission limits and fuel-switching incentives.

policy_statement: Kuwait will use tree planting, citizen education, and public awareness to reduce the impacts of future temperature and precipitation changes.
source_quote: Some recommended efforts to minimize the effect of these changes are tree plantings to decrease the albedo, educating citizens and raising public awareness about climate changes consequences.
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete adaptation-oriented response to projected climate impacts. It qualifies as policy because it identifies specific interventions, though it is somewhat broad and not framed as a formal mandate.

policy_statement: Kuwait will design an adaptation plan to address climate change impacts on human settlements and natural environments.
source_quote: The coastal zone of Kuwait is also expected to be affected by sea level rise (SLR), one of the major consequences of global climate change. (KEPA, INC, 2012) revealed that about 65 thousand people would be exposed to SLR risk and more than 240 km 2  of land (1.35% of Kuwait's land) would be inundated when sea level increases only 0.5 m: These lands include vital services and infrastructures, such as hospitals, educational institutions, and major ports. Thus, designing an adaptation plan to face climate change, which has already observed, is a mandatory task to ensure the sustainability of human settlements and natural environments of Kuwait.
extraction_rationale: This is a direct adaptation planning commitment tied to a specific hazard. It qualifies as policy because it calls for an adaptation plan in response to sea level rise.

policy_statement: Kuwait will conduct climate vulnerability assessments to identify vulnerable sectors, understand climate risks, and develop strategies to reduce vulnerability.
source_quote: CVAs also illustrate links between climate change factors (e.g., elevated temperature  and  sea  level  rise)  and  non-climate  factors  (e.g.,  population  growth  and corruption): Understanding these links would assist societies to improve their capacity building for climate change (Kim, Calzada, Scott, & Zermoglio, 2018). Such efficient CVAs require systematic methods to be delivered.
extraction_rationale: This is a methodological adaptation commitment. It qualifies because it establishes a systematic assessment process to support adaptation planning.

policy_statement: Kuwait will use GIS-based climate vulnerability mapping to rank risks and identify the most vulnerable places to climate change.
source_quote:
The ranked weighted layers are then spatially overlaid to compute the sum of weighted scores. This process produced a CVI layer for each sector. These layers are weighted with the same manner to calculate the overall CVI map illustrating the vulnerable places to climate change: The highest pixel values in the CVI map revealed the most vulnerable

places to climate change.
section_header: 3.3.1 An Overview of the CVI method
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete analytical policy tool for adaptation planning. It qualifies because it specifies a method for identifying vulnerability hotspots.

policy_statement: Kuwait will use climate risk ranking criteria to prioritize adaptation options and identify urgent climate risks.
source_quote: Assessing ranks of climate risks and vulnerabilities is a critical step in conducting CVI. It is  also  a  fundamental  component  in  prioritizing  adaptation  options  and  illustrating vulnerabilities  of  sectors  to  climate  change  in  a  comprehensive  context.  The  ranking process is complex and subjective relying on qualitative analysis and experts' opinions (Aldababseh, et al., 2018).
extraction_rationale: This is a planning and prioritization commitment. It qualifies as policy because it establishes a decision framework for adaptation prioritization.

policy_statement: Kuwait will implement adaptive coastal land-use policies that restrict major projects on vulnerable coasts.
source_quote: One of the feasible mitigation options to this risk is to apply an adaptive coastal land use policy that restricts establishing major projects on vulnerable coasts. This risk received a weighted sum score of 4.35 due to the severe impact that can cause (Table 12).
extraction_rationale: This is a specific land-use policy intended to reduce sea-level-rise exposure. It qualifies because it is a regulatory planning measure with a clear adaptation function.

policy_statement: Kuwait will establish national health alerts for dust events and heat waves and adjust working hours to reduce health risks.
source_quote:
Some recommendations that could improve the adaptation capacity in the health sector are adjusting the official working hours during the summer season, raising awareness on how to respond to extreme events and designing  national health alert for dust storm (KEPA, SNC, 2019).

The  geographic  distribution  of  asthma  patients  in  Kuwait's  urban  districts.  The  area shaded in the grey color are either residential areas with no patients' data recorded during the study time or non-residential areas (KEPA, INC, 2012).
extraction_rationale: This is a direct adaptation measure responding to heat and dust hazards. It qualifies because it specifies alerts and work-hour adjustments to reduce health impacts.

policy_statement: Kuwait will implement green belts and expand protected areas to adapt to dust storms.
source_quote: Kuwait has undertaken some adaptation projects such as implementing green belts project and increasing the protected areas to adapt to a dust storm. The green belt projects consist of planted areas with trees and shrubs of 50-180 Km in length and 5-20 Km in width. These projects have started in 2015 for 5-year duration time.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific adaptation intervention with a clear hazard focus. It qualifies because it involves planted buffers and protected areas to reduce dust storm impacts.

policy_statement: Kuwait will develop new crop varieties and landscape trees that can tolerate high temperatures, salinity, and drought.
source_quote: Development of new varieties of crops that can adapt to high temperatures  and  have  high  resistance  to  salinity  and  drought  such  as  Conocarpus, Ficus,  Prosopis,  and  date  palm  trees,  were  implemented  in  Kuwait  (Al  Dosery  et  al., 2012). These types of plants are mainly planted in Wafraa and Abdali, Kuwait.
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete adaptation intervention in agriculture and landscaping. It qualifies because it specifies climate-resilient crop development and deployment.

policy_statement: Kuwait will establish eMISK as a comprehensive geo-environmental database and GIS system to support environmental data updating and analysis.
source_quote: The eMISK  aims  at building and maintaining a comprehensive geo-environmental database of Kuwait and a GIS  system  to  facilitate  updating  and  analyzing  environmental  data.  While  beatona initiative  aims  to  increase  public  awareness  through  sharing  real-time  environmental news and information.
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete institutional and information-system commitment supporting adaptation planning. It qualifies because it establishes a named system with ongoing operational function.

policy_statement: Kuwait will establish the Kuwait Green Wall Project to plant 315,000 trees along a 420 km border wall to hold back moving sand.
source_quote: Meanwhile, Kuwait has implemented a project called 'Kuwait Green Wall Project. This project aims to increase the protected areas by planting 315,000 trees for 420 Km wall along the borderline to hold back the moving sand. The adaptation sector is the Public Health/ Dust Control, and the responsible parties are the governments and NGOs.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific, quantified nature-based adaptation project. It qualifies because it sets a clear intervention, scale, and climate hazard purpose.

policy_statement: Kuwait will establish a food security program with projects in fisheries management, water resource management, natural resource management, animal production, animal health, and technical capacity development.
extraction_rationale: This is a programmatic adaptation commitment with named sectors and interventions. It qualifies because it establishes a structured food security initiative linked to climate resilience.

policy_statement: Kuwait and FAO will establish a regional database and information center to support fisheries management and aquaculture development.
source_quote:
Establishment of a regional database and information center to support the fisheries management and aquaculture development , a joint project between PAAFR in Kuwait and FAO in December 2016. The project aims at establishing a regional database and information center to support the fisheries management and aquaculture development

in the region.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific institutional project supporting adaptation in fisheries and aquaculture. It qualifies because it creates a named information infrastructure.

policy_statement: Kuwait will establish fisheries farms using brackish water to support food security.
source_quote: Fisheries  Farms .  Fisheries  are  considered  a  vital  source  of  food  in  Kuwait.  The establishment of fisheries farms is an important step to adapt to climate change under the food security sector. Nile tilapia (Oreochromis niloticus) culture is implemented in agriculture  farms  where  crops  such  as  alfa  alfa,  tomatoes,  potatoes,  onions  are cultivated.
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete adaptation project in food security. It qualifies because it specifies a named intervention and climate adaptation purpose.

policy_statement: Kuwait will assess historic climate records and future climate projections through a project led by Kuwait University and UN Environment.
source_quote: Assessment of historic climate records and future projection .  The project aimed at assessing the historic climate records for the past 70 years and make future projection climatic  scenarios  until  the  year  2100.  The  project  started  in  2012  by  the  Kuwait University and UN Environment.
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete analytical adaptation project. It qualifies because it establishes a climate data and projection effort for planning.

policy_statement: Kuwait will establish eMISK Industry to collect an environmental inventory of industrial facilities.
source_quote: eMISK Industry ; this project aims at establishing a national program for collecting an environmental inventory of industrial facilities in Kuwait. The Adaptation Sector for this project is Public Health.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific information-system project with environmental management relevance. It qualifies because it is a named program with a defined operational objective.

policy_statement: Kuwait will establish eMISK Waste to manage industrial liquid waste vehicles and logistics.
source_quote: eMISK Waste ; this project aims at finding and implementing a solution to be able to manage  the  fleet  of  industrial  liquid  waste  vehicles  and  organizing  the  logistics process. The Adaptation Sector for this project is the Waste Sector.
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete operational waste-management project. It qualifies because it specifies a named system and implementation objective.

policy_statement: Kuwait will establish eMISK Marine to support policies and programs for integrated coastal and ocean management.
source_quote: eMISK Marine ; The project aims at promoting and facilitating information management system in support of policies and programs that enhance integrated coastal and ocean management  in  Kuwait.  The  Adaptation  Sector  for  this  project  is  the  Coastal Zones/SLR.
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete information-management project supporting coastal adaptation. It qualifies because it is a named system tied to coastal management.

policy_statement: Kuwait will continue constructing desalination plants and water distribution systems to protect freshwater sources and maintain ecological stability.
source_quote: Building desalination plants .  In the process of protecting freshwater sources and to maintain  ecological  stability.  Kuwait  has  constructed  several  desalination  plants  in addition to water distribution systems via pipelines and irrigation systems to farmers. In 2016, Kuwait produced around 3.85 MCM/d of desalinated water.
extraction_rationale: This is a major infrastructure investment in water supply. It qualifies because it is a named public investment line with climate adaptation relevance.

policy_statement: Kuwait will invest jointly with MIT to update current desalination plants and develop next-generation desalination plants.
source_quote: Kuwait is investing USD 5.5 million jointly with MIT to conduct researches on updating the current desalination plants and next-generation desalination plants . The adaptation Sector for this project is the Water Resources Sector, and the Government is responsible for the implementation of this project since 2016 and it is still ongoing.
extraction_rationale: This is a funded technology-development commitment. It qualifies because it includes a specific investment and adaptation-related infrastructure research.

policy_statement: Kuwait will teach rural households in-house water desalination techniques to provide freshwater at low cost and short time.
source_quote: Education on household desalination .  Kuwait jointly with United Nations taught the Kuwaiti  people  in  rural  areas  the  'in-house  water  desalination  techniques',  where households can have freshwater at low cost and short time. The Adaptation Sector for this project is the Water Resources and the Awareness sectors.
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete capacity-building and technology-transfer initiative. It qualifies because it is a named intervention aimed at water resilience.

policy_statement: Kuwait will implement KIEIN-IV as a GIS-based environmental information network to compile indicators, disseminate data, and support climate monitoring and adaptation.
source_quote:
Kuwait Integrated Environmental Information Network Phase-IV . The KIEIN-IV is an integrated GIS-based system that compiles the environmental indicator data and acts as a spatial decision support system tools (SDSS). This project can:
- Compile data about environmental indicators for Kuwait.

- Expand  and  enhance  the  KIEIN  GIS  website  as  an  environmental  data dissemination tool.
- Promote awareness and usage of the KIEIN GIS website toward protecting Kuwaiti habitats.
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete information-system and decision-support project. It qualifies because it supports adaptation monitoring and planning.

policy_statement: Kuwait will implement the Kuwait Environmental Governance Initiative to support the National Adaptation Plan and related initiatives in water, city planning, and other sectors.
source_quote: Kuwait Environmental Governance Initiative (KEGI) . The Project supports the design of the National Adaptation Plan (NAP) of Kuwait and the relevant initiatives linked to water, city planning, and other sectors. This project was running from 2017-2018 by the UNDP and EPA with a budget of $2,000,000.
extraction_rationale: This is a funded governance and planning initiative directly tied to adaptation. It qualifies because it supports NAP design and sectoral initiatives.

policy_statement: Kuwait will establish land and marine nature reserves to safeguard marine and land ecosystems.
source_quote: Establishment of land and marine nature reserves .  The project aims to establish a series of land and marine nature reserves in the State of Kuwait. National reserves were  implemented  to  safeguard  the  Kuwait  marine  and  land  ecosystems.
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete ecosystem-protection measure. It qualifies because it establishes protected areas as climate adaptation infrastructure.

policy_statement: Kuwait will apply water conservation technologies to reduce water consumption by 20 percent.
source_quote: Water Conservation (Partially implemented) Kuwait's Initial National Communications ; the application of  water conservation technologies was also one of the adaptation options  to  reduce  water  consumption by  20  %.  The Water  Resources  Sector  was responsible, and the project started in 2012 and is still ongoing.
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified resource-efficiency measure with adaptation relevance. It qualifies because it states a specific reduction target and technology intervention.

policy_statement: Kuwait will establish a Coastal Information System to protect coastal zones and marine environments and support planners and decision makers.
source_quote: Establishing a Coastal information system (CIS) ;  Coastal Information System (CIS) was established to help in the protection of coastal zones and marine environments in  Kuwait.  CIS provides  information  about  Kuwait's  coastal  area  to  planners  and decision makers.
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete adaptation information system for coastal management. It qualifies because it is a named system with a clear protective function.

policy_statement: Kuwait will construct tidal barriers in new developments to protect against erosion and rising sea levels.
source_quote: Constructing tidal barriers in new developments ; Sabah Al Ahmad Sea City, which is located near the Saudi Arabia border, is a new development which constructed a tidal gate system and offshore breakwater was built to protect the artificial promenade from erosion  of  waves  and  to  cope  with  the  rising  sea  levels  as  the  adverse  impact  of climate change.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific adaptation infrastructure measure. It qualifies because it directly addresses sea-level rise and erosion.

policy_statement: Kuwait will conduct awareness campaigns and symposiums to increase public and stakeholder awareness of sea level rise adaptation.
source_quote: Conducting awareness campaigns and symposiums regarding Sea level rise ; the 'Our Seas: Theories, Data, and Policies' Symposium highlighted the importance of human intervention regarding rising sea levels. International specialists, local researchers, and  non-governmental  organizations  attended  this  symposium.
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete awareness and outreach initiative tied to climate adaptation. It qualifies because it is a named campaign with a clear adaptation objective.

policy_statement: Kuwait will implement the Coastal Management Program to produce integrated coastal zone management and best-practice guidelines for coastal development.
source_quote: Coastal  Management  Program ;  the  CMP  produces  physical  modeling,  numerical modeling  and  field  survey  measurements.  The  CMP  was  responsible  to  produce Integrated Coastal Zone Management (ICZM) for Kuwait. The ICZM consists of two phases, Phase 1 has already completed.
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete planning and management program for coastal adaptation. It qualifies because it establishes a named program with implementation outputs.

policy_statement: Kuwait will implement the Water Resources Development and Management Program to optimize water use and develop integrated water policies and action plans.
source_quote: Establishment of the Water Resources Program ; A water resources development and management program (WRDM) was initiated by the Kuwait Institute for Science and Research (KISR). This program helps to identify ways to optimize the water resources use and management through applied research. WRDM program was designed to develop integrated  water  policies,  management options,  and action  plans  to  solve water  scarcity  problems  and  increase  Kuwait's  water  security  and  resilience.
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete adaptation program with policy and planning outputs. It qualifies because it is a named program aimed at water security and resilience.

policy_statement: Kuwait will use multi-stage flash desalination technology to expand desalination capacity.
source_quote: Constructing Desalination using Multi-Stage Flash technology ; Kuwait has a total of 40  operating  Multi-Stage  Flash  desalination  units  (MSF),  with  a  total  production capacity of 234 MGD. The project was completed by the Government and the MEW under the Technology Needs Assessment / Water Resources Sectors.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific technology deployment in water supply infrastructure. It qualifies because it is a named intervention with climate adaptation relevance.

policy_statement: Kuwait will research wastewater treatment and reclamation technologies to reuse wastewater for irrigation.
source_quote: Wastewater Treatment and Reclamation Technologies Program ;  this  program  has been initiated by KISR and it aims at conducting research on reclaiming and reusing Kuwait's wastewater to utilize it in irrigation purposes. This is a good example to adapt to climate change stresses on water resources.
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete resource-efficiency and adaptation measure. It qualifies because it targets wastewater reuse for irrigation.

policy_statement: Kuwait will conduct awareness campaigns on KEPA Articles 76 and 79 regarding ambient air quality compliance and emission source evaluation.
source_quote: Awareness Campaign of KEPA Articles 76 and 79; an awareness campaign has been conducted to increase the awareness about Article No. 76 regarding the ambient air and Air Quality Zone Compliance actions and Article No. 79 regarding the emission sources and evaluation. The responsible parties for this project were the EPA and the UNDP  and  the  adaptation  sectors  for  this  project  were  the  Technology  Needs Assessment / Public Health sectors.
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete awareness and compliance initiative. It qualifies because it supports implementation of environmental rules with climate and air-quality relevance.

policy_statement: Kuwait will maintain the Beatona Initiative as a public awareness website sharing real-time environmental news and information.
source_quote: Beatona Initiative ;  Beatona  Initiative  is  a  website  established  by  EPA  and  aims  to increase the public awareness of the health sector of the climate change adaptation through sharing real-time environmental news and information with the public.
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete public-awareness initiative supporting adaptation. It qualifies because it is a named ongoing platform with a climate-related communication function.

policy_statement: Kuwait will implement the Tarsheed Campaign to reduce per-capita electricity and water consumption.
source_quote: Tarsheed Campaign ; Tarsheed campaign was an Initiative made to reduce the percapita  consumption  of  electricity  and  water.  This  awareness  initiative  is  a  good adaptation step to climate change in water resources.
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete demand-reduction initiative. It qualifies because it targets electricity and water consumption, though the climate link is partly indirect.

policy_statement: Kuwait will implement the Tarsheed Campaign II to encourage reduce, reuse, and recycle waste management.
source_quote: Tarsheed Campaign II ; Tarsheed campaign II was an Initiative to encourage  the implementation of the 'Reduce, Reuse and Recycle' waste management. Such an initiative is useful as a climate change adaptation under the waste sector.
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete waste-management initiative with resource-efficiency benefits. It qualifies because it promotes the 3Rs, though the climate link is indirect.

policy_statement: Kuwait will use treated sewage effluent from Umm Al-Hayman WWTP for irrigation purposes.
source_quote: Utilizing TSE water generated from Umm Al-Hayman WWTP in Irrigation purposes ; TSE  is  utilized  to  irrigate  the  green  areas  and  agricultural  areas  and  serve  the expected population growth of Kuwait, in addition, to mitigate the negative effects on the environment. The Ministry of Public Works (MPW) held this project from 20122018 under the Water Resources Sector.
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete water-reuse measure. It qualifies because it reuses treated wastewater for irrigation and reduces pressure on freshwater resources.

policy_statement: Kuwait will restrict outdoor work from 11:00 AM to 4:00 PM during June through August.
source_quote: Adjust the official working hours Initiative Source :  the Ministry of Social Affairs and Labor of Kuwait issued a national law in 2005 to stop any outdoor work from 11:00 AM to 16:00 PM during the months of June through August. The EPA started this project in 2018 under the Public Health Sector.
extraction_rationale: This is a binding labor regulation with a clear heat adaptation purpose. It qualifies because it sets a specific time restriction to reduce heat exposure.

policy_statement: Kuwait will support preparation of its Second National Communication and Biennial Update Report to the UNFCCC.
source_quote: Enabling Kuwait to Prepare it's Second National Communication (SNC) and Biennial Update  Report  (BUR)  to  the  UNFCCC ;  the  project  aims  at  supporting  Kuwait  to prepare  and  deliver  its  Second  National  Communication  and  first  Biennial  Update Report. The project also enables Kuwait to fulfill its UNFCCC obligations.
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete reporting and compliance project. It qualifies because it supports formal climate reporting obligations.

policy_statement: Kuwait will implement the Environmental Pollution and Climate Program to assess pollution and climate change challenges across atmospheric, aquatic, and terrestrial environments.
source_quote: The  Environmental  Pollution  and  Climate  (EPC)  Program ;  this  program  aims  at  assessing the pollution and climate change challenges concerning the atmospheric, aquatic, and terrestrial environment of Kuwait. This project is still ongoing under the responsibility of KISR.
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete ongoing program with climate and environmental assessment functions. It qualifies because it is a named program with a defined objective.

policy_statement: Kuwait will collect and recycle empty plastic bottles instead of sending them to landfills.
source_quote: Omniya Plastic bottles recycle ;  an  initiative  to  collect  the  empty  plastic  bottles and recycling it instead of sending to landfills which is one of few practical initiatives to adapt to climate change in waste sectors. The project started in 2015 by an NGO and is still ongoing under the Waste Sector.
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete waste-reduction and recycling initiative. It qualifies because it specifies a named recycling action with climate relevance.

policy_statement: Kuwait has ratified the UNFCCC, Kyoto Protocol, Paris Agreement, UNCCD, and other environmental conventions and protocols.
source_quote: Kuwait has ratified some agreements  and  policies  in  climate  change  adaptation  such  as  UNFCCC, Kyoto Protocol, UN Convention on the Law of the Sea, FAO Compliance Agreement and Paris Agreement on climate change. Table 17 provides the main policies and strategies on adaptation to climate change that were ratified by Kuwait.
section_header: 4.3 Policies and Strategies on Climate Change Adaptation
extraction_rationale: This is a set of formal international commitments. It qualifies as policy because ratification creates binding or quasi-binding obligations, though the climate relevance varies by instrument.

policy_statement: Kuwait will monitor biological diversity and build the institutional structure needed to address biodiversity issues.
source_quote: CBD Ratification                                                                       | Monitor the biological diversity of Kuwait. Build the necessary institutional structure to deal with biodiversity issues in Kuwait 36 . | General   |   2002   | EPA/Kuwait / UNDP |
section_header: 4.3 Policies and Strategies on Climate Change Adaptation
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete institutional and monitoring commitment tied to biodiversity governance. It qualifies because it specifies monitoring and institutional development.

policy_statement: Kuwait will enforce Environment Protection Law No. 42/2014 to address climate change impacts, protect land and soil, reduce desertification, manage natural reserves and water resources, and create disaster management plans.
source_quote: Environment Protection Law No. 42/2014   | Adapting to the adverse impacts of climate change. The protection of land and soil, reducing desertification, management of natural reserves and water resources and creating plans for disaster management.      | General/ Safety and Health | 2014   | The Environmen tal Public Authority / Environmen tal Supreme Council / / Kuwait |
section_header: 4.3 Policies and Strategies on Climate Change Adaptation
extraction_rationale: This is a binding legal instrument with explicit climate adaptation content. It qualifies because it mandates protection, management, and disaster planning.

policy_statement: Kuwait will regulate any activity that may pollute the environment through Law No. 16/1996 establishing the Environmental Public Authority.
source_quote: Law No. 16/1996                          | Established the Kuwait Environmental Public Authority and gave it the power to regulate any activity that may pollute the environment                                                                             | General / Environme nt     | 1996   | EPA / Kuwait                                                                    |
section_header: 4.3 Policies and Strategies on Climate Change Adaptation
extraction_rationale: This is a regulatory environmental law with climate relevance through pollution control. It qualifies because it creates institutional regulatory authority.

policy_statement: Kuwait will protect the environment, require environmental impact assessment for projects, control pollution-causing activities, and minimize environmental pollution under Article 3.
source_quote: Article 3                                | Protects the Environment, evaluates the Environmental Impact Assessment Studies projects before implementation, controls activities that may lead to pollution, and combats and minimizes environmental pollution | Environme ntal             |        | EPA / Kuwait                                                                    |
section_header: 4.3 Policies and Strategies on Climate Change Adaptation
extraction_rationale: This is a regulatory environmental policy with pollution-control and planning functions. It qualifies because it imposes EIA and pollution control requirements.

policy_statement: Kuwait will make polluters responsible for rehabilitation actions under Article 13.
source_quote: Article 13                               | Enforces that the pollution, whether person or a factory, shall be responsible for and pay for any rehabilitation actions.                                                                                        | General                    |        | EPA/Kuwait                                                                      |
section_header: 4.3 Policies and Strategies on Climate Change Adaptation
extraction_rationale: This is a regulatory polluter-pays rule. It qualifies because it assigns responsibility and payment obligations for environmental rehabilitation.

policy_statement: Kuwait will tackle environmental problems in industrial areas under Decision Number 6/2004.
source_quote: Decision Number 6/2004                   | Tackles problems concerning the environment in the industrial area.                                                                                                                                               | General   | 2004   | EPA/ Kuwait                                                                     |
section_header: 4.3 Policies and Strategies on Climate Change Adaptation
extraction_rationale: This is a regulatory or administrative environmental measure. It qualifies because it is a formal decision addressing industrial environmental problems.

policy_statement: Kuwait will allocate financial resources, integrate the NAP into sectoral strategies and action plans, and create staff or units to coordinate mainstreaming of climate adaptation.
source_quote: The National governmental institutions will advance the implementation of the NAP by allocating the needed financial resources, integrating the NAP into sectoral strategies and action plans as well as into other projects and initiatives; designating staff or may be creating new unit(s) with adequate staff and resources to coordinate the mainstreaming and integration of the  NAP  and other  relevant  strategies  into  the  national  institutions' mandates.
extraction_rationale: This is a clear implementation and resource-allocation commitment. It qualifies because it specifies institutional and financial measures for NAP delivery.

policy_statement: KEPA will set targets, coordinate actions for resilience and adaptive capacity, and prepare climate reporting documents.
source_quote: The Kuwait Environment  Public Authority  (KEPA) as the principal government  institution  acting  as  independently  to  carry  out  environmental actions  in  Kuwait,  the  lead  agency  of  the  government  on  national  climate change actions, and delivery of operational coordination,  shall  report  to  the Cabinet through the Director of KEPA. Among other several actions, KEPA is working  on  setting  targets  and  coordinate  actions  for  building  resilience  to climate  change  and  enhancing  adaptive  capacity;  developing  the  National Determined Contribution (NDC) Report and preparing and submitting the SNC report.
extraction_rationale: This is a direct institutional implementation commitment with specific outputs. It qualifies because it assigns KEPA target-setting and reporting responsibilities.

policy_statement: The Supreme Council for Planning and Development will mainstream climate adaptation into state strategic goals and development plans and propose a financial mechanism for sectoral adaptation plans.
source_quote: The SCPD shall, among others, ensure the mainstreaming of climate change adaptation  actions  by  other  national  agencies,  ensure  that  climate  change adaptation  plans  are  mainstreamed  in  the  State's  strategic  goals  and  the designed  development  strategies  and  plans,  and  propose  an  appropriate financial mechanism to ensure implementation of the sectoral adaptation plans.
extraction_rationale: This is a clear institutional policy and financing commitment. It qualifies because it mandates mainstreaming and a financial mechanism.

policy_statement: Kuwait will develop vulnerability and risk assessment reports, provide open access to information networks, build capacity, and review projects for coastal adaptation.
source_quote: Short-term actions                | ▪ Develop vulnerability and risk assessment reports ▪ Provide open access for information and communication networks for parties and sectors responsible ▪ Capacity-building for government and non- government stakeholders on the deployment of adaptation activities. ▪ Increase decision-makers awareness of the risks of SLR and the damages to nearby urban areas. ▪ Review existed projects and update them based on SNC and NAP findings.
section_header: 5.3.3 Adaptation Plans to enhance the resilience of the Coastal Zone
extraction_rationale: This is a set of concrete short-term adaptation actions. It qualifies because it specifies assessment, communication, capacity-building, and review measures.

policy_statement: Kuwait will provide financial aid for coastal protection, ensure resources for coastal projects, and legislate restrictions on negative coastal activities.
source_quote: Medium-term actions   | ▪ Provide financial aid for preventative and protective actions for coastal damage. ▪ Make sure that the required resources to undergo projects and initiatives concerning the construction, research or communication are available. ▪ Raising awareness among decision-makers in Kuwait to incorporate SLR scenarios into development plans ▪ Legislating laws to restrict negative anthropogenic activities in the coastal zones to maintain the coastal wildlife
section_header: 5.3.3 Adaptation Plans to enhance the resilience of the Coastal Zone
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete adaptation package combining finance, regulation, and awareness. It qualifies because it includes resource allocation and legal restrictions.

policy_statement: Kuwait will establish a specialized center for coastal management, construct protection barriers, and strengthen coastline protection laws and policies.
source_quote: Long-term actions     | ▪ Establish a specialized center for coastal management and build and organize information and tools for climate risk modeling and generation of qualified responses within the Coastal Zone. ▪ Protect coastlines from SLR by constructing protection barriers. ▪ Develop better and more intensive laws and policies regarding coastline protection and conservation. ▪ Prepare for better adaptation potential for future setbacks and scenarios (i.e. new construction projects near the high-risk coastline should withstand SLR scenario in the future).
section_header: 5.3.3 Adaptation Plans to enhance the resilience of the Coastal Zone
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete long-term adaptation strategy with institutional, structural, and regulatory components. It qualifies because it specifies multiple deliberate interventions.

policy_statement: Kuwait will increase public awareness, conduct climate-health risk assessments, adjust working hours, establish health alerts, develop warning systems, and create a climate and health research network.
source_quote:
Short term actions                | ▪ Increase public awareness of climate changes effects and impacts on general health. ▪ Conduct risk assessments and vulnerability to Climate Change on the general public. ▪ Involve the media in carrying the message of issues of Health, as people get more influenced and receive the message more directly and subconsciously through advertisement and social media sites.

|                     | ▪ Adjust the official working hours to avoid working during maximum temperatures in the day (study and issue a new threshold). ▪ Raising awareness of how to respond to dust and heat waves events. ▪ Establishing national health alerts for dust storms and heat waves.   |
|---------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Medium-term actions | ▪ Develop warning systems for extreme weather conditions combined with a communication strategy for alerts. ▪ Increase drought-proof vegetation to reduce dust fallout from dust storms.                                                                                    |
| Long-term actions   | ▪ Include information and instructions about Climate Change Effects on Health in the early education curriculum. ▪ Establish a research and monitoring network on climate and health, with a focus on analyzing the expected climate change impact on health.               |
section_header: 5.3.4 Adaptation Plans to enhance the resilience of the Human Health Sector
extraction_rationale: This is a set of concrete health adaptation actions spanning awareness, alerts, planning, and research. It qualifies because it includes multiple specific interventions and institutional measures.

policy_statement: The City will proactively adapt to growth while improving equity and quality of life for all residents.
source_quote: This Plan provides a strategic framework for the City to proactively adapt to growth while improving equity and quality of life for all residents.
section_header: A CITY AT AN INFLECTION POINT
extraction_rationale: This is a clear planning commitment with an adaptation objective tied to growth pressures and quality of life. It is somewhat broad, but it is still a stated strategic policy direction.

policy_statement: The Master Plan will serve as a resilience strategy focused on proactive planning around population health and key resources, beginning with water.
source_quote: At its core, the 2050 Master Plan is a resilience strategy focused on smart and proactive planning around population health and key resources, beginning with water. Water is central to any consideration of public health, economic strength and quality of life in Las Vegas.
extraction_rationale: This is a direct resilience planning commitment centered on climate-sensitive resource management. It is policy-like because it defines the plan's core strategy, though it is framed at a high level.

policy_statement: The City will use land use planning to reduce water demand and heat island impacts.
source_quote: It sets forth a vision of creative and forward-thinking land use planning to improve health outcomes, reduce water demand and heat island impacts, and improve quality of life for all Las Vegas residents today and in the future.
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete climate adaptation commitment because it explicitly targets water demand and urban heat island impacts through planning.

policy_statement: The City will acknowledge climate change and heat island effects as threats and incorporate resiliency and climate action/adaptation into land-use planning, policies, and standards.
source_quote:
Acknowledge both heat island effect and climate change are threats.

Intentionally incorporate key issues of resiliency and climate action/adaptation into all land-use planning, policies, and standards.
extraction_rationale: This qualifies as a policy because it directs incorporation of climate adaptation into planning and standards. The language is broad, but it is a deliberate governance commitment.

policy_statement: The City will use smart growth development practices to protect limited resources and mitigate the urban heat island.
source_quote: Protect the environment for future generations and mitigate urban heat island by using smart growth development practices to protect and maintain limited resources.
extraction_rationale: This is a policy because it specifies a planning approach intended to reduce heat risk and conserve resources. It is somewhat general, but the climate objective is explicit.

policy_statement: The City will increase density in key parts of the city where it improves access to efficient energy, transportation, and community resources.
source_quote: Increase density. Density will occur in key parts of the city based on analysis which shows the biggest increases in access to efficient energy, transportation, and community resources.
extraction_rationale: This is a planning commitment with a specific land-use intervention. It is primarily resource efficiency because it emphasizes efficient energy, transportation, and resource access.

policy_statement: The City will prioritize and incentivize construction of Missing Middle housing to create more affordable housing that efficiently uses natural resources.
source_quote: Prioritizing and incentivize construction of 'Missing Middle' housing will create more affordable housing which efficiently uses natural resources and matches the character of Las Vegas neighborhoods.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific intervention and includes an incentive-oriented commitment. It is primarily resource efficiency because the mechanism is efficient land/resource use, not emissions reduction.

policy_statement: The City will optimize the efficient use of limited land and water by promoting enhanced infrastructure, increased tree shade, and strategic density along transportation corridors.
source_quote: Efficiently use resources. Optimize the efficient use of limited resources such as land and water by promoting practices such as enhanced city infrastructure, increased tree shade, and strategic density along transportation corridors.
extraction_rationale: This is a clear resource-efficiency policy with named interventions. Tree shade also has adaptation co-benefits, but the primary mechanism is efficient resource use.

policy_statement: The City will shift land use strategy toward infill and redevelopment as land supply declines.
source_quote: The plan for existing and future land use recognizes that land supply will greatly reduce over the next thirty years. As existing development agreements and new subdivisions are completed in the western and northwestern part of the City, this plan recognizes the need to shift to a strategy of infill and redevelopment.
extraction_rationale: This is a planning commitment to a specific development strategy. It is climate-relevant indirectly through compact development and reduced land consumption.

policy_statement: The City will prioritize higher-density development along mixed-use transit-oriented development corridors and integrate diverse affordable housing types.
source_quote: To accomplish an infill strategy that ties with many additional goals throughout the plan, the plan links identified regional centers with mixed-use transit-oriented development (TOD) corridors, accented at key nodes. These corridors must be prioritized for higher density development that integrates a diverse range of affordable housing types.
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete land-use and housing policy with a clear implementation direction. It is primarily resource efficiency because it promotes compact, transit-oriented development.

policy_statement: The City will amend Title 19 and its zoning typology to support the new land use framework.
source_quote: A number of new place types are recommended, as well as a corresponding land use tool-box, zoning typology, and modest amendments to Title 19, including:
extraction_rationale: This is a regulatory commitment because it contemplates code amendments to implement the plan. The climate relevance is indirect, as the code changes support broader land-use and resource goals.

policy_statement: The City will preserve and maintain established traditional neighborhoods, key buildings, and landmarks while allowing adaptive reuse.
source_quote: The Land Use strategy strives to ensure established traditional neighborhoods, key buildings, and landmarks are preserved and well maintained, while also providing flexibility for property owners to make adaptive reuse.
extraction_rationale: This is a preservation and land-use policy with a specific intervention. It is not primarily climate-focused, but it supports efficient reuse of existing assets.

policy_statement: The City will reduce heat hazards through green infrastructure and tree canopy expansion, including zoning amendments and planting at least 100,000 native and adaptive trees to raise canopy cover to 20%.
source_quote:
Due to notable increases in the urban heat island effect, steps must be taken to reduce heat hazards with appropriate green infrastructure, including:

- LVMC and zoning amendments for trees
- At least 100,000 public and private high quality, native and adaptive trees that increase the canopy are planted to increase the canopy to 20%
extraction_rationale: This is a direct adaptation policy with a quantifiable target and a regulatory mechanism. It also uses ecological infrastructure as the adaptation mechanism.

policy_statement: The City will develop a Parks System Plan, achieve CAPRA certification, increase park acreage to 7 acres per 1,000 residents, and ensure 85% of dwelling units are within a short walk of a park or trail.
source_quote:
Because parks and recreational facilities are an important quality of life component, park facilities, amenities, connections, and safety were frequently noted throughout public outreach. As a result, the City will

- Develop  a  Parks  System  Plan  and  achieve  CAPRA certification
- Increase park acreage to 7 acres per 1,000 residents, specifically in noted areas of need
- Ensure 85% of dwelling units are within a short walk of a park or trail
extraction_rationale: This is a policy package with measurable targets and a planning action. It is primarily nature-based solutions because parks and trails function as green infrastructure, with adaptation co-benefits.

policy_statement: The City will eliminate food deserts, reduce food swamps, and increase access to healthy food and community gardens while allowing small agricultural uses.
source_quote:
Given  the  lack  of  regional  agriculture,  it  is  necessary to ensure supply chain security and redundancy. To supplement these efforts, the City must ensure:

- No food deserts and reduce food swamps by increasing healthy food access
- Provide accessibility to community gardens and increase allowable small agricultural uses
