To ensure that City government is doing its part, the Mayor and City Council directed the Office of Sustainability & Environment to update the Seattle Climate Action Plan (CAP) outlining actions City government should take in the near- and long-term to achieve our community climate action goals.

The 2013 CAP provides a coordinated strategy for action that cuts across City functions, and focuses on City actions that reduce GHG emissions while also supporting other community goals, including building vibrant neighborhoods, fostering economic prosperity, and enhancing social equity.
extraction_rationale: This is a governing commitment to produce and implement a city climate plan with defined purpose and scope. It is policy-like because it directs an agency to update the plan and sets the framework for subsequent actions.

policy_statement: Seattle's climate vision is to reach zero net greenhouse gas emissions by 2050 and prepare for the likely impacts of climate change.
source_quote:
In 2011, recognizing that the Kyoto Protocol goal is just the first step forward in reducing climate pollution, the Mayor and City Council adopted a bold climate protection vision for our community (through Resolution 31312): 21%

- Reach Zero Net Greenhouse Gas (GHG) Emissions by 2050
- Prepare for the likely impacts of climate change
extraction_rationale: This is a formal target adopted by resolution, satisfying the quantifiable target criterion. It combines mitigation and adaptation goals, but the primary framing is a citywide climate target.

policy_statement: The City will monitor implementation of 2015 and 2030 actions annually, track outcome indicators every other year, and report local community greenhouse gas inventories every three years.
source_quote:
The Office of Sustainability & Environment will be responsible for monitoring and reporting on the progress of the 2013 CAP's targets and actions on the following schedule:

- Implementation of 2015 Actions & 2030 Actions: Annually. (The following pages summarize actions to implement by 2015 and identify the lead implementing agency for each action.)
- Climate Action Outcome Indicators: Every other year, or as data is available. See table of indicators below. Note: There are several challenging gaps in data. Specifically, the lack of a City of Seattle Transportation model to provide city-specific travel data is a significant barrier to accessing transportation related Climate Action Outcome indicators and GHG information.
- Local Community GHG Emissions: Every three years, including inventories for 2012 & 2015. 2012's inventory is currently under way.
extraction_rationale: This is an operational monitoring commitment with a defined reporting schedule. It qualifies as policy because it establishes ongoing implementation oversight and accountability.

policy_statement: The City will renew and extend the Bridging the Gap levy and prioritize investments in transit, pedestrian, cycling improvements, and system maintenance.
source_quote:
Renew and extend the time frame of the Bridging the Gap levy and prioritize investments in transit, pedestrian, and cycling improvements and system maintenance.

Secure local or transit agency authority to levy a motor vehicle excise tax (MVET) at the City or County level.
extraction_rationale: This is a funding commitment tied to transportation infrastructure and maintenance. It is a broad financial instrument because it concerns a levy and dedicated investment priorities.

policy_statement: The City will seek authority to levy a motor vehicle excise tax at the City or County level.
source_quote:
Secure local or transit agency authority to levy a motor vehicle excise tax (MVET) at the City or County level.

Work with regional and state partners to adopt a funding strategy to meet current and future transportation needs.
extraction_rationale: This is a proposed tax authority, which is a financial instrument intended to fund transportation needs. It is clearly policy because it seeks enabling authority for a revenue mechanism.

policy_statement: The City will work with regional and state partners to adopt a funding strategy to meet current and future transportation needs.
source_quote:
Work with regional and state partners to adopt a funding strategy to meet current and future transportation needs.

Begin construction of 23rd Avenue priority bus corridor.
extraction_rationale: This is a planning and financing commitment for transportation infrastructure. It is policy because it directs intergovernmental action toward a funding strategy.

policy_statement: The City will begin construction of the 23rd Avenue priority bus corridor.
source_quote:
Begin construction of 23rd Avenue priority bus corridor.

Complete the preliminary engineering and environmental analysis for the Center City Transit Connector.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific infrastructure project with a clear implementation action. It qualifies as policy because it commits to construction.

policy_statement: The City will complete preliminary engineering and environmental analysis for the Center City Transit Connector.
source_quote:
Complete the preliminary engineering and environmental analysis for the Center City Transit Connector.

Develop a Freight Master Plan that includes goals to make freight movement more efficient and reduce its impact on greenhouse gas emissions.
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete project-development commitment. It qualifies as policy because it directs a defined planning and environmental review action.

policy_statement: The City will develop a Freight Master Plan to make freight movement more efficient and reduce its impact on greenhouse gas emissions.
source_quote:
Develop a Freight Master Plan that includes goals to make freight movement more efficient and reduce its impact on greenhouse gas emissions.

Build bicycle lanes that are physically separated from traffic in the Center City.
extraction_rationale: This is a named planning initiative with an explicit emissions-reduction goal. It is policy because it directs creation of a master plan with climate-related objectives.

policy_statement: Singapore will reduce its emissions intensity by 36 per cent below 2005 levels by 2030 and stabilise emissions with the aim of peaking around 2030.
source_quote:
We aim to reduce our emissions intensity by 36 per cent below 2005 levels by 2030 and stabilise our emissions with the aim of peaking around 2030.

Climate Action Plan : Take Action Today, For a Carbon-Efficient Singapore sets out four strategies to achieve this.
extraction_rationale: This is a clear quantified national climate commitment with a deadline, so it qualifies as a policy target.

policy_statement: Singapore will continue to improve energy efficiency across industry, transport, buildings, households, waste, and water sectors through awareness-building, enhanced regulations, capability building, and government support.
source_quote: Improving energy efficiency will remain our key strategy for reducing emissions across the industry, transport, buildings, household, waste, and water sectors. Increased awareness building, enhanced regulations, capability building, and government support will help Singapore achieve this.
extraction_rationale: This is a broad strategic commitment with named mechanisms for implementation, even though it is not a single numeric target.

policy_statement: Singapore will reduce carbon emissions from power generation by adopting more efficient technologies and increasing the share of non-fossil fuels in the electricity mix.
source_quote: At the same time, we will reduce carbon emissions from power generation . We will aim to adopt more efficient technologies and increase the share of nonfossil fuels in our electricity mix.
extraction_rationale: This is a direct mitigation commitment with specific interventions in the power sector.

policy_statement: Singapore will continue to develop and demonstrate low-carbon technologies and scale up low-carbon solutions for deployment in Singapore and for export overseas.
source_quote: We will continue to develop and demonstrate cutting-edge lowcarbon technologies as well as scale up low-carbon solutions for deployment in Singapore and export overseas. This will position us well to tap on global and regional green growth opportunities.
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete technology-development and deployment commitment, supported by a stated implementation direction.

policy_statement: Singapore will pursue collective climate action by government agencies, individuals, businesses, and the community, alongside mitigation and adaptation efforts.
source_quote: We must respond to the challenges of climate change as one nation, through the collective action of government agencies, individuals, businesses, and the community . Our efforts to mitigate carbon emissions, coupled with steps taken to adapt to climate change 1 , will ensure that Singapore remains a vibrant and liveable city for current and future generations.
extraction_rationale: This is a broad policy direction rather than a specific program, but it is still a stated commitment to collective climate action.

policy_statement: Singapore pledged to reduce emissions by 16 per cent from business-as-usual levels by 2020.
source_quote:
In 2009, Singapore pledged to reduce emissions by 16 per cent from business-as-usual (BAU) levels by 2020.

In 2015, building on our earlier commitment, Singapore pledged to reduce our Emissions Intensity 11  (EI) by 36 per cent from 2005 levels by 2030, and stabilise emissions with the aim of peaking around 2030.
section_header: SINGAPORE'S COMMITMENTS TO ADDRESS CLIMATE CHANGE
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified emissions-reduction pledge with a deadline.

policy_statement: Singapore pledged to reduce emissions intensity by 36 per cent from 2005 levels by 2030 and stabilise emissions with the aim of peaking around 2030.
source_quote: In 2015, building on our earlier commitment, Singapore pledged to reduce our Emissions Intensity 11  (EI) by 36 per cent from 2005 levels by 2030, and stabilise emissions with the aim of peaking around 2030.
section_header: SINGAPORE'S COMMITMENTS TO ADDRESS CLIMATE CHANGE
extraction_rationale: This is a clear national mitigation target with a deadline and quantified reduction.

policy_statement: Singapore will continue to pursue higher levels of energy efficiency, including deployment of best-in-class technologies, to support its emissions stabilisation goal.
source_quote: Singapore plans to further reduce our emissions intensity as part of international efforts to address climate change. For a very small country with limited alternative energy options, the stabilisation of our emissions with the aim of peaking around 2030 requires serious efforts by everyone. We have to strive for higher levels of energy efficiency, including deployment of best-in-class technologies. '
extraction_rationale: This is a policy direction tied to a climate target, though it is somewhat general and lacks a separate numeric target.

policy_statement: Singapore will continue to study the optimal mix of policies and technologies to achieve its 2030 pledge and remain responsive to local and global developments.
source_quote: The above strategies will guide our work as we study the optimal mix of policies and technologies to achieve our 2030 commitment. We will remain nimble and responsive to local and global developments, to identify appropriate and effective measures that will reduce emissions and increase our energy efficiency.
extraction_rationale: This is a planning commitment supporting implementation of the 2030 pledge, though it is somewhat process-oriented.

policy_statement: Singapore will improve industrial energy efficiency, reduce non-CO2 greenhouse gases from industrial processes, and adopt cleaner fuels.
source_quote:
- Increase industrial energy efficiency
- Reduce non-CO 2 GHGs from industrial processes
- Adopt cleaner fuels
extraction_rationale: These are explicit sectoral mitigation actions listed as part of the national strategy.

policy_statement: Singapore will achieve BCA Green Mark standards for 80 per cent of buildings by 2030, improve energy efficiency of building tenants, and improve energy efficiency of data centres.
source_quote:
- Achieve BCA Green Mark standards for 80 per cent of buildings by 2030
- Improve energy efficiency of building tenants
- Improve energy efficiency of data centres
extraction_rationale: This is a set of concrete building-sector commitments with a quantified target and named interventions.

policy_statement: Singapore will raise Minimum Energy Performance Standards for household appliances, introduce MEPS for more appliances, encourage adoption of efficient appliance models, and introduce smart home technology.
source_quote:
- Raise Minimum Energy Performance Standards (MEPS) for household appliances and introduce MEPS for more appliances
- Encourage adoption of efficient appliance models
- Introduce smart home technology
extraction_rationale: This is a clear resource-efficiency policy package with regulatory and technology measures.

policy_statement: Singapore will achieve 75 per cent use of public transport by 2030, encourage cycling and walking, and improve vehicle fuel efficiency.
source_quote:
- Achieve 75 per cent use of public transport by 2030
- Encourage cycling and walking
- Improve vehicle fuel efficiency
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified transport-efficiency and modal-shift commitment with a deadline.

policy_statement: Singapore will reduce plastics incineration and improve energy efficiency in desalination and used water treatment.
source_quote:
- Reduce plastics incineration
- Improve energy efficiency in desalination and used water treatment
extraction_rationale: This is a sectoral resource-efficiency commitment with specific interventions.

policy_statement: Singapore will reduce its emissions intensity by 36 per cent from 2005 levels by 2030 and stabilise emissions with the aim of peaking around 2030.
source_quote: To reduce our Emissions Intensity (EI) by 36 per cent from 2005 levels by 2030, and stabilise emissions with the aim of peaking around 2030.
extraction_rationale: This repeats the national pledge as a standalone statement and qualifies as a quantified climate target.

policy_statement: Singapore will improve industrial energy efficiency, reduce non-CO2 greenhouse gases from industrial processes, and adopt cleaner fuels in industry.
source_quote:
## Industry

- Increase industrial energy efficiency
- Reduce non-CO 2 GHGs from industrial processes
- Adopt cleaner fuels
extraction_rationale: This is a direct sectoral mitigation policy package with specific actions.

policy_statement: Singapore will achieve BCA Green Mark standards for 80 per cent of buildings by 2030, improve energy efficiency of building tenants, and improve energy efficiency of data centres.
source_quote:
## Buildings

- Achieve BCA Green Mark standards for 80 per cent of buildings by 2030
- Improve energy efficiency of building tenants
- Improve energy efficiency of data centres
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified building-sector policy with specific efficiency measures.

policy_statement: Singapore will raise MEPS for household appliances, introduce MEPS for more appliances, encourage efficient appliance models, and introduce smart home technology.
source_quote:
## Household

- Raise Minimum Energy Performance Standards (MEPS) for household appliances and introduce MEPS for more appliances
- Encourage adoption of efficient appliance models
- Introduce smart home technology
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete regulatory and technology package for household energy efficiency.

policy_statement: Singapore will achieve 75 per cent use of public transport by 2030, encourage cycling and walking, and improve vehicle fuel efficiency.
source_quote:
## Transport

- Achieve 75 per cent use of public transport by 2030
- Encourage cycling and walking
- Improve vehicle fuel efficiency
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified transport modal-shift and efficiency commitment.

policy_statement: Singapore will reduce plastics incineration and improve energy efficiency in desalination and used water treatment.
source_quote:
## Water and Waste

- Reduce plastics incineration
- Improve energy efficiency in desalination and used water treatment
extraction_rationale: This is a specific resource-efficiency commitment in the water and waste sectors.

policy_statement: The Energy Conservation Act will be reviewed regularly so that it remains effective in supporting energy efficiency improvements.
source_quote: The Energy Conservation Act (ECA), which covers energy-intensive industrial firms, will be reviewed regularly so that it remains effective in supporting energy efficiency improvements.
section_header: INCREASING INDUSTRIAL ENERGY AND CARBON EFFICIENCY
extraction_rationale: This is a regulatory commitment to maintain and strengthen an existing climate-related law.

policy_statement: Singapore will support greater energy efficiency through schemes already in place and by seeking feedback on possible new initiatives to improve manufacturing sector energy efficiency.
source_quote: Several schemes are already in place to support greater energy efficiency (see next page). In the first half of 2016, NEA sought feedback from companies on existing schemes and on possible new initiatives, to improve manufacturing sector energy efficiency.
section_header: INCREASING INDUSTRIAL ENERGY AND CARBON EFFICIENCY
extraction_rationale: This is a policy implementation and consultation commitment, though somewhat process-oriented.

policy_statement: The Singapore Certified Energy Manager programme will provide training and certification in energy management, with a grant covering about 70 per cent of training costs.
source_quote: This is a training and certification programme in energy management. The SCEM training grant covers about 70 per cent of training costs.
section_header: SCHEMES TO HELP COMPANIES ACHIEVE GREATER ENERGY EFFICIENCY
extraction_rationale: This is a capacity-building program with a financial support component, qualifying as a policy instrument.

policy_statement: Energy-intensive industrial users must appoint an energy manager, monitor and report energy use and GHG emissions-related information annually, and submit and review an energy efficiency improvement plan annually.
source_quote: Energy-intensive users in the industrial sector are required to appoint an energy manager, monitor and report energy use and GHG emissions-related information annually. They also have to submit an energy efficiency improvement plan and review this plan annually.
section_header: SCHEMES TO HELP COMPANIES ACHIEVE GREATER ENERGY EFFICIENCY
extraction_rationale: This is a binding regulatory requirement with clear compliance obligations.

policy_statement: The Energy Efficiency National Partnership Programme will promote energy management systems, organise learning events, and provide recognition schemes to encourage best practices in energy management.
source_quote:
This is a voluntary partnership programme for companies that includes:

- Promoting adoption of an energy management system (For example, ISO 50001)
- Organising learning events such as the National Energy Efficiency Conference
- Providing recognition schemes to encourage best practices in energy management
section_header: SCHEMES TO HELP COMPANIES ACHIEVE GREATER ENERGY EFFICIENCY
extraction_rationale: This is a named program with specific actions to improve energy efficiency, though voluntary.

policy_statement: The Energy Efficiency Financing Pilot Programme will finance up to 100 per cent of the upfront capital investment of energy efficiency projects.
source_quote: Under this programme, companies receive financing for up to 100 per cent of the upfront capital investment of energy efficiency projects. Cost savings are shared between the financier and the company.
extraction_rationale: This is a broad financial instrument supporting energy efficiency investments.

policy_statement: NEA will co-fund up to 50 per cent of the cost of design workshops to integrate energy and resource efficiency in new facilities, capped at $600,000 per project.
source_quote: NEA co-funds up to 50 per cent of the cost of design workshops to integrate energy and resource efficiency in the design of new facilities, capped at $600,000 per project.
extraction_rationale: This is a direct subsidy/grant for efficiency-oriented design work.

policy_statement: NEA will co-fund 50 per cent of the costs of energy audits, capped at $200,000 per project.
source_quote: NEA co-funds 50 per cent of the costs of an energy audit, which assesses energy consumption and helps to develop energy efficiency improvement plans for existing facilities, capped at $200,000 per project.
extraction_rationale: This is a financial incentive supporting energy efficiency improvements.

policy_statement: EDB and NEA will co-fund up to 20 per cent of the investment cost of energy efficient equipment or technologies.
source_quote: EDB and NEA co-fund up to 20 per cent of the investment cost of energy efficient equipment or technologies.
extraction_rationale: This is a direct subsidy for energy-efficient capital investment.

policy_statement: Singapore will study policy options to support measures and technologies that reduce non-CO2 greenhouse gas emissions from the semiconductor sub-sector.
source_quote: EDB and NEA will study policy options to support the implementation of appropriate measures and technologies to reduce non-CO 2 GHG emissions from the sub-sector.
extraction_rationale: This is a policy-development commitment aimed at emissions reduction, though it is exploratory rather than immediate.

policy_statement: Singapore will study policy options to facilitate the switch from fuel oil to cleaner fuels such as natural gas in industry.
source_quote: EDB and NEA will study further policy options to facilitate this switch.
extraction_rationale: This is a policy study commitment supporting a specific emissions-reduction intervention.

policy_statement: BCA revised the Green Mark 2015 criteria to raise energy performance standards and increase recognition for energy efficiency and renewable energy adoption.
source_quote: To keep pace with technological advancements and raise energy performance standards, BCA introduced the revised Green Mark 2015 criteria. Enhancements include increased recognition for energy efficiency and for adoption of renewable energy.
section_header: ACHIEVING GLOBAL LEADERSHIP IN GREEN BUILDINGS
extraction_rationale: This is a regulatory/standards update for green buildings with explicit climate-related mechanisms.

policy_statement: BCA will step up efforts to encourage retrofitting of tenanted spaces with energy-efficient fittings and support zero-capital energy efficiency retrofits for buildings.
source_quote: Beyond the existing Green Lease Toolkit 20  and user-centric Green Mark schemes, BCA will step up efforts to encourage the retrofitting of tenanted spaces with energy-efficient fittings, such as light fittings. To enhance current efforts to green existing buildings, BCA and Singapore Green Building Council (SGBC) have collaborated to develop the Zero Capital Partnership 21  scheme, which provides a 'zero capital' solution for building owners to carry out energy efficiency retrofits for buildings.
section_header: Building a Greener Tomorrow 3rd Green Building Masterplan
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete implementation commitment with a named retrofit scheme and efficiency objective.

policy_statement: Singapore aims to make 80 per cent of all buildings green by 2030.
source_quote: These efforts will contribute to Singapore's aim of making 80 per cent of all buildings green by 2030.
section_header: Building a Greener Tomorrow 3rd Green Building Masterplan
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified building-sector target with a deadline.

policy_statement: IDA will implement initiatives to encourage energy efficiency in the design, operation, and management of data centres, including standards, Green Mark certification, investment allowances, and the Green Data Centre Programme.
source_quote: Recognising this, IDA has implemented initiatives to encourage energy efficiency in the design, operation, and management of data centres. This includes the Green Data Centre Standard (Singapore Standard 564), the BCAIDA Green Mark for Data Centres, the Investment Allowance scheme for energy efficiency projects and the Green Data Centre Programme (GDCP) that supports high-impact research, development, and demonstration projects on energy efficiency in data centres.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific sectoral policy package with standards, incentives, and programmatic support.

policy_statement: Singapore will trial electric vehicles in fleet-based operations and introduce up to 1,000 EVs and 2,000 charging kiosks through an EV car-sharing pilot programme.
source_quote: In the second phase, the use of EVs will be trialled for fleet-based operations. An EV car-sharing pilot programme for this phase will introduce as many as 1,000 EVs and an island-wide charging infrastructure comprising up to 2,000 charging kiosks to support the eventual proliferation of EVs.
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete pilot program with quantified deployment and infrastructure targets.

policy_statement: IDA and SPRING Singapore announced a $20 million pilot project to develop an integrated delivery system for malls to reduce trucks on the road and lower carbon emissions.
source_quote: In 2015, IDA and SPRING Singapore announced a $20 million pilot project to develop an integrated delivery system for malls. If scaled to cover all of Singapore's malls, such consolidation and coordination could reduce the number of trucks on the road by 25 per cent, reduce waiting time for deliveries by 65 per cent, reduce the manpower required for deliveries by 40 per cent, and result in lower carbon emissions from trucks.
extraction_rationale: This is a funded pilot project with explicit emissions-reduction and logistics-efficiency outcomes.

policy_statement: Singapore will use the Carbon Emissions-based Vehicle Scheme to incentivise low-emission cars and penalise high-emission cars and taxis through upfront rebates and surcharges.
source_quote: Under the CEVS, these vehicles are divided into categories based on their CO 2 /km performance. Low-emission cars are given incentives, while high-emission cars incur a penalty in the form of a registration surcharge. The rebate or surcharge for taxis is 50 per cent higher than cars as taxis generally clock a higher mileage and thus typically emit more CO 2 per year than cars.
section_header: ENCOURAGING THE SHIFT TO MORE EFFICIENT VEHICLES
extraction_rationale: This is a clear financial instrument and regulatory incentive scheme aimed at reducing vehicle emissions.

policy_statement: The Fuel Economy Labeling Scheme will provide fuel-performance information to help consumers choose fuel-efficient cars.
source_quote: The Fuel Economy Labeling Scheme (FELS) introduced in 2012 complements the CEVS by providing information on the fuel performance of each car model. Together, the CEVS and FELS allow consumers to choose fuel-efficient cars, which in turn leads to savings on fuel cost and lower carbon emissions.
section_header: ENCOURAGING THE SHIFT TO MORE EFFICIENT VEHICLES
extraction_rationale: This is a named informational policy supporting lower-emission vehicle choice.

policy_statement: NEA will progressively raise minimum standards for appliances to increase market efficiency while preserving product availability and consumer choice.
source_quote: The minimum standards for appliances will be progressively raised to increase the efficiency of the appliances on the market , while ensuring that product availability and consumer choice are not adversely affected. This will also result in lower lifecycle costs for consumers.
extraction_rationale: This is a regulatory standard-setting commitment with a clear implementation direction.

policy_statement: NEA will consider including other appliances under the Mandatory Energy Labelling Scheme in the future and will continue public campaigns to promote energy-efficient appliances.
source_quote:
NEA will consider including other appliances in the future.

In addition to schemes like MEPS and MELS, NEA will continue to promote energy-efficient appliances through public messaging campaigns - such as the 'Save Energy Save Money' initiative - at retail outlets, HDB void decks, and through social media.
section_header: Promoting and Increasing Awareness about Energy Efficient Appliances
extraction_rationale: This is a policy commitment to expand labeling coverage and continue awareness campaigns.

policy_statement: HDB and IDA will pilot Home Energy Management Systems in selected households in Yuhua to assess feasibility for larger-scale implementation.
source_quote:
HEMS are currently being piloted in selected households in the Yuhua estate to assess the feasibility of larger scale implementation.

The Yuhua pilot programme, led by HDB and IDA and in partnership with PUB, NEA, and MOH, will assess the usefulness and user-friendliness of HEMS.
extraction_rationale: This is a named pilot program with a clear implementation objective.

policy_statement: PUB will pilot new desalination and used-water technologies to halve energy use in seawater desalination and reduce carbon emissions from the water sector.
source_quote: PUB is pilot testing new technologies such as electrochemical desalting, with the aim of halving the energy used in the seawater desalination process. Improved technologies for reclaiming used water could also reduce energy use. These reductions in energy use would decrease carbon emissions from the water sector.
extraction_rationale: This is a specific technology pilot with a quantified energy-saving goal and climate benefit.

policy_statement: NEA will pilot district-level collection and processing of food waste for anaerobic co-digestion with used water sludge at Ulu Pandan Water Reclamation Plant.
source_quote: NEA is also conducting a pilot programme to evaluate the economic viability and feasibility of the district-level collection and processing of food waste for anaerobic co-digestion 25  with used water sludge at the Ulu Pandan Water Reclamation Plant.
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete pilot program involving waste-to-energy/resource recovery, though the climate objective is somewhat indirect.

policy_statement: NEA aims to increase the overall recycling rate from 61 per cent in 2015 to 70 per cent in 2030.
source_quote: NEA aims to increase the overall recycling rate from 61 per cent in 2015 to 70 per cent in 2030, by increasing awareness and implementing other policy initiatives (see feature story).
section_header: Increasing Energy and Carbon Efficiency in the Waste Management Process
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified waste-sector target with a deadline.

policy_statement: PUB will build a demonstration-scale Integrated Validation Plant at Ulu Pandan Water Reclamation Plant to test technologies for the future Tuas Water Reclamation Plant.
source_quote: PUB is building a demonstration-scale Integrated Validation Plant within its Ulu Pandan Water Reclamation Plant (WRP) to test new technologies for potential implementation at the future Tuas WRP. The aim is to make the Tuas WRP more eco-friendly, enabling it to consume less energy than conventional plants and produce more biogas for power generation.
section_header: ENHANCING ENERGY EFFICIENCY OF TUAS WATER RECLAMATION PLANT
extraction_rationale: This is a specific demonstration project with an efficiency and energy-recovery objective.

policy_statement: NEA will continue the National Recycling Programme, require centralised chutes for recyclables in new HDB developments, mandate waste data and waste reduction plans for large hotels and shopping malls, and support the Singapore Packaging Agreement to reduce packaging waste.
source_quote: The National Recycling Programme was launched by NEA in 2001 to make recycling more convenient for households. All new HDB developments launched from 2014 will be fitted with Centralised Chutes for Recyclables. NEA has also made it mandatory for large hotels and shopping malls to submit waste data and waste reduction plans. In addition, NEA has worked with the industry and non-governmental organisations to get various parties to sign the voluntary Singapore Packaging Agreement that aims to reduce packaging waste, which constitutes about one-third of Singapore's domestic waste.
section_header: INITIATIVES TO REDUCE WASTE AND INCREASE EFFICIENCY IN THE WASTE SECTOR
extraction_rationale: This is a package of regulatory and programmatic waste-reduction measures with clear implementation elements.

policy_statement: HDB Greenprint will transform Yuhua into a smart and sustainable estate through energy and water conservation, waste management, greenery enhancement, and eco-living initiatives.
source_quote: In the next stage of development, Yuhua will be further transformed into a smart and sustainable estate through various initiatives. These include the introduction of smart home solutions as part of HDB's Smart Enabled Home Initiative.
section_header: HOUSING & DEVELOPMENT BOARD (HDB) GREENPRINT IN YUHUA ESTATE
extraction_rationale: This is a place-based sustainability program with multiple concrete interventions, though not all are strictly climate-specific.

policy_statement: Singapore will continue to improve energy efficiency across all sectors and may study carbon pricing to encourage lower energy consumption and adoption of efficient technologies.
source_quote:
Energy efficiency will continue to be Singapore's key strategy for reducing carbon emissions across all sectors. We will require everyone, including businesses and the community, to make adjustments to their daily activities, choices, and processes. To do so, greater access to information on energy use and best practices will be provided to guide businesses and individuals towards making informed decisions.

The government will also review and enhance incentives, regulations, and capability-building programmes in order to drive energy efficiency improvements.
extraction_rationale: This is a broad forward-looking policy commitment with multiple implementation levers.

policy_statement: Singapore will study the need to price carbon to enhance efforts across all sectors.
source_quote: As part of this, we will be studying the need to price carbon to enhance efforts across all sectors. A carbon price would send appropriate price signals to encourage changes in energy consumption, provide market incentives for the adoption of energy-efficient technologies and low-carbon solutions, and stimulate growth in green industries.
extraction_rationale: This is a clear policy study commitment on a carbon-pricing instrument, though it is not yet an adopted measure.

policy_statement: Singapore will invest in research and development to study new technologies that can boost energy efficiency in the longer term.
source_quote: In addition, we will invest in research and development to study new technologies that can boost energy efficiency in the longer term (see Chapter 4 for more details).
extraction_rationale: This is a public investment commitment supporting climate-related innovation.

policy_statement: EMA will work with power generation companies to encourage adoption of more efficient technologies.
source_quote: The Energy Market Authority (EMA) will work with power generation companies to encourage them to adopt more efficient technologies. This will lower their production costs, reduce carbon emissions and keep prices competitive for electricity consumers.
extraction_rationale: This is a sectoral implementation commitment aimed at reducing emissions through efficiency.

policy_statement: Singapore will raise solar adoption in its system to 350MWp by 2020 and support the SolarNova programme through deployment, R&D, policy enhancements, and engagement.
source_quote:
Singapore plans to raise the adoption of solar power in our system to 350MWp by 2020, representing about 5 per cent of peak electricity demand. A key initiative aimed at developing the solar industry in Singapore is the SolarNova programme. Falling prices and continued market demand are expected to accelerate the adoption of solar energy.

Agencies like BCA, EMA, EDB, and NEA will study ways to support this development and sustain the momentum generated by the SolarNova programme, through encouraging the deployment of solar PV systems on buildings, continued investments in solar R&D, policy enhancements, and engagement efforts with various sectors to promote solar adoption.
section_header: INCREASING RENEWABLE ENERGY: SOLAR PHOTOVOLTAIC (PV) SYSTEMS
extraction_rationale: This is a quantified renewable-energy target plus a supporting programmatic commitment.

policy_statement: Singapore will invest in research on solar forecasting, energy storage, and smart grids to support a higher share of intermittent renewable electricity.
source_quote: Solar energy generation is intermittent as it is affected by variable factors such as cloud cover. To support an increasing share of intermittent electricity generation, Singapore will invest in research efforts in solar forecasting, energy storage, and smart grids.
section_header: INCREASING RENEWABLE ENERGY: SOLAR PHOTOVOLTAIC (PV) SYSTEMS
extraction_rationale: This is a specific research investment commitment supporting renewable integration.

policy_statement: HDB will call solar leasing tenders of around 30 to 50MW approximately every nine to 12 months on behalf of government agencies.
source_quote: HDB will structure and call for solar leasing tenders of around 30 to 50MW approximately every nine to 12 months on behalf of various government agencies.
extraction_rationale: This is a concrete procurement/tender commitment supporting solar deployment.

policy_statement: PUB and EDB will test-bed a floating solar PV system on Tengeh Reservoir and study its impacts on evaporation, biodiversity, and water quality.
source_quote: PUB and EDB are test-bedding a floating solar PV system on Tengeh Reservoir which can generate up to 3.3GWh of electricity per annum, equivalent to the average annual energy consumption of 750 HDB households. At a cost of $11 million, the project will also assess the impact of solar PV deployment on reservoir evaporation, biodiversity and water quality.
extraction_rationale: This is a funded demonstration project with a renewable-energy objective and explicit environmental assessment.

policy_statement: Singapore will continue to study technologies that increase power generation efficiency and support greater adoption of alternative energy, while monitoring nuclear technologies and building nuclear science capabilities.
source_quote: Singapore will continue to study technologies that can increase the efficiency of power generation and support increased adoption of alternative energy. Singapore conducted a nuclear energy pre-feasibility study, which concluded that current nuclear energy technologies were not yet suitable for deployment in Singapore. We will continue to monitor the progress of nuclear technologies and build capabilities to understand nuclear science and technology.
extraction_rationale: This is a forward-looking technology and capability-building commitment, though partly exploratory.

The $470 million Environment and Water Technologies - Clean Water Strategic Research Programme (SRP) was established in 2006 to support innovation in smart and energy-efficient water technologies, to address Singapore's need for water security.

The $365 million Clean Energy SRP was established in 2007 with an initial emphasis on solar energy. It was renamed in 2011 as the Energy SRP to cover additional domains such as smart grids, green buildings, and power utilities. The Energy SRP established two energy research centres to support the growth of the clean energy industry, namely the Solar Energy Research Institute of Singapore (SERIS) and the Energy Research Institute @ Nanyang Technological University (ERI@N).

The Energy National Innovation Challenge (ENIC) was established in 2011 to develop and deploy cost-competitive energy solutions within 20 years that would improve Singapore's energy efficiency, reduce carbon emissions, and broaden our energy options. Funding of $300 million was set aside between 201 1 and 2015 for such solutions, covering areas such as green buildings, green data centres, energy storage, and waste-to-energy.
